text: {"question":"What observational technique and spectral diagnostics does the study employ to determine the chemical composition of stars within the JAGB selection box, and how do these results quantify the level of oxygen‑rich contamination reported in the abstract?","reference_answer":"The survey uses optical spectroscopy covering 3590–7150 Å, capturing nine molecular bandheads (six TiO and three C₂ Swan). By measuring bandhead‑step indices, the authors classify each star as carbon‑rich or oxygen‑rich, finding that only 13 of the 54 JAGB‑box stars are carbon‑rich, implying a 71 % oxygen‑rich contamination."}
